scope: First-use A paragraph plus presentation staging of eight existing BCD tasks. Broader curriculum walkthrough remains in progress.

changes.originalPrompt: A human primary spermatocyte has replicated its DNA. State chromosome number and duplication at the start, after meiosis I and after meiosis II. Add one distinct hormonal support pathway.
stages: Stage and count reasoning: a human primary spermatocyte has replicated its DNA. State chromosome number and duplication at the start, after meiosis I and after meiosis II.
Hormonal support: add one distinct hormonal support pathway.

changes.originalPrompt: Construct four separate hormone graphs from the supplied six-day table. Choose labelled axes and an appropriate scale, then enter every point. Explain the estrogen–LH sequence and the later progesterone change. State one limitation of sparse, separately scaled indices.
stages: Set up four separate hormone graphs from the supplied six-day table. Choose labelled axes and an appropriate scale for each hormone.
Plot: enter every point from the table.
Explain: describe the estrogen–LH sequence and the later progesterone change.
Limit: state one limitation of sparse, separately scaled indices.

changes.originalPrompt: For AaBb × AaBb with independently assorting loci and complete dominance, calculate P(aabb) and P(A_bb). Explain each multiplication.
stages: Use AaBb × AaBb, independently assorting loci and complete dominance. Calculate P(aabb) and explain the multiplication.
Calculate P(A_bb) and explain the multiplication.

changes.originalPrompt: Under a fully penetrant autosomal recessive model, two unaffected parents have an affected child. Give parent genotypes and the carrier probability for another child known to be unaffected.
stages: Use a fully penetrant autosomal recessive model: two unaffected parents have an affected child. Give the parent genotypes.
For another child known to be unaffected, calculate the carrier probability.

changes.originalPrompt: An AB/ab heterozygote is test-crossed with ab/ab, producing 40 AB, 40 ab, 10 Ab and 10 aB gamete-derived offspring. Calculate recombination frequency. In a separate mapping dataset, interpret distances A–B=14, B–C=6 and A–C=20 map units.
stages: Recombination dataset: an AB/ab heterozygote is test-crossed with ab/ab, producing 40 AB, 40 ab, 10 Ab and 10 aB gamete-derived offspring. Calculate recombination frequency.
Separate mapping dataset: interpret distances A–B=14, B–C=6 and A–C=20 map units.

changes.originalPrompt: Given coding DNA 5′-ATGGAATTTTAA-3′, write aligned template DNA and the mRNA 5′→3′. Explain which strand RNA polymerase reads.
stages: Given coding DNA 5′-ATGGAATTTTAA-3′, write the aligned template DNA.
Write the mRNA 5′→3′.
Explain which strand RNA polymerase reads.

changes.originalPrompt: In 100 diploid organisms, AA=36, Aa=48 and aa=16. Calculate p and q from counts, calculate the Hardy–Weinberg expectations and state which calculation needs model assumptions.
stages: From counts: in 100 diploid organisms, AA=36, Aa=48 and aa=16. Calculate p and q.
From the model: calculate the Hardy–Weinberg expectations.
Assumptions: state which calculation needs model assumptions.

changes.originalPrompt: Use the three explicitly separate datasets. For quadrats 2, 8, 4, 10 and 6 plants in five 1 m² samples from 200 m², calculate density and estimated abundance. For initial N=1000, B=120, I=30, D=70 and E=20 in ten days, calculate absolute rate and interval per-capita change. Then plot both supplied growth-model series on common labelled axes and explain why they diverge.
stages: Quadrat estimate: use 2, 8, 4, 10 and 6 plants in five 1 m² samples from 200 m². Calculate density and estimated abundance.
Separate demographic dataset: initial N=1000, B=120, I=30, D=70 and E=20 in ten days. Calculate absolute rate and interval per-capita change.
Separate growth-model dataset: plot both supplied series on common labelled axes.
Model comparison: explain why the two growth-model series diverge.
